text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx + websocket disconnect rate for tenant "evergreen-capital" (vpc-gateway us-east-1). Detected spike at 18:14 UTC, creating incident thread.
incident-bot: Incident ID INC-2026-6010 created, severity=P2, paging Rao (oncall). Link: https://internal.incidents/INC-2026-6010
Rao: Ack'ing. I'm on it. Marta can you pull proxy logs and concurrent connection graphs?
Marta (eng-sre): Pulling now. Immediate observations: concurrent ws conns for tenant jumped from ~380 -> ~1.9k within 40s. Backend dedicated pool nodes started returning 502s and some accept() failures (EMFILE) on a subset of nodes. Sample excerpts:
```
2026-04-02T18:13:58Z gw-proxy[gw-12]: tenant=evergreen conn=0x7f1f accept: EMFILE
2026-04-02T18:14:01Z gw-proxy[gw-12]: tenant=evergreen backend=dedicated-evg-2 status=502
2026-04-02T18:14:02Z lb[lb-4]: route: tenant=evergreen spilled->shared-gw
```
Marta (eng-sre): Note: there was a maintenance hotpatch to shared-gw at 18:10 UTC (keepalive tuning + accept backlog change). If spillover happened, that could explain higher drop rates.
Liz (acct-eng): Customer report: "we suddenly lost ~15% of live quotes for ~5 minutes, then client retried aggressively causing duplicates". They say their client retries every 1.5s with no jitter. They're asking for immediate mitigation.
Dmitri (eng-runtime): If nodes are hitting EMFILE, we can either raise ulimit and epoll limits, or reduce acceptance rate at the front door (throttle). Recommend: 1) pin tenant to dedicated pool to avoid shared runtime behavioral changes, 2) scale dedicated pool +2 nodes, 3) bump ulimit on dedicated pool nodes, 4) push a short lived per-tenant smoothing limiter.
Rao: Agreed. Marta, do you have the control-plane command to pin? I'll take the pin.
Marta (eng-sre): Commands:
```
# pin tenant to dedicated pool
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/evergreen-capital/route -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"pin_pool":"dedicated-evg-2"}'
# create smoothing limiter
curl -X POST https://gw-config.internal/v1/limits -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant":"evergreen-capital","type":"ws_smoothing","rate":250,"burst":600,"ttl_sec":3600}'
# bump node ulimit (or schedule config rollout)
kubectl -n dedicated-evg patch daemonset evg-proxy --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"evg-proxy","securityContext":{"privileged":false},"resources":{}}]}}}}'
```
Marta (eng-sre): Applying pin now.
Rao: Applying pin and limiter. Executing scale next.
Rao: :gear: Pin applied (controlplane returned 200). Rollout id r-evg-309. Observability: https://console.redwood/observability/r-evg-309
ops-bot: Scale request accepted for deployment dedicated-evg-2 -> +2 replicas. New replica scheduling.
Marta (eng-sre): After pin + limiter + scale request: error rate declined ~65% within 90s, EMFILE events stopped on pinned nodes. Some clients still report single-frame loss; chasing a code path where an EPIPE on write does not trigger frame requeue. Filing GW-909.
Dmitri (eng-runtime): We'll pick up GW-909. Short-term: can we push a tiny keepalive/idle increase on the pool proxies to reduce perceived timeouts?
Marta (eng-sre): Patching gw-proxy config for dedicated-evg-2: keepalive 45s -> 90s, idleTimeout 60s -> 180s.
Rao: Pushed keepalive change. Monitoring.
Liz (acct-eng): Customer changed client behavior to exponential backoff with jitter (base 4s) per our ask; they report fewer duplicates. They still want an RCA and SLA impact calc.
Marta (eng-sre): Metrics: after all mitigations (pin, scale, limiter, keepalive) connection success rate back to ~98% and CPU on pool nodes down from 92% -> 58%. Impact window ~18:13:55 - 18:20:40 UTC (~7m).
Dmitri (eng-runtime): Initial hypothesis: combination of aggressive client retries -> tenant spike -> spillover to shared cluster which had recent accept/backpressure tuning. Shared nodes rejected or reset connections faster leading to transfer of load back to dedicated pool and transient EMFILE. Code-level issue causing lost frames on transient write failures exacerbated customer-visible data loss.
Rao: Handoff: Marta will own monitoring and post-incident activities; Dmitri to own GW-909 and runtime patch. We need follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: patch to requeue frames on transient write errors (GW-909).
- eng-platform: consider a guardrail to prevent immediate spillover when tenant's burst > X within Y seconds.
- client-advise: account-eng to propose recommended jitter/backoff and include in customer integration doc.
Marta (eng-sre): I'll schedule the RCA walkthrough and produce a short postmortem. Planning meeting tomorrow 09:30 PST with eng-runtime + eng-platform + acct-eng.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-6010 status -> MONITORING (owner: Marta). Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime (Dmitri).
Rao: Closing the active pager. If error rate rises again, re-alert oncall. :thumbsup:
Liz (acct-eng): Customer appreciated quick action; requesting follow-up call to discuss SLA credit. I'll coordinate.
Dmitri (eng-runtime): Noted GW-909 and adding integration test against heavy reconnect churn in chaos suite.
Marta (eng-sre): Adding runbook note: when a tenant spills, immediately check for recent shared-gw changes and consider automatic temporary pin + scale before allowing shared->dedicated oscillation.
Rao: Thanks team. Incident summary to status page and customer comms in progress.
